judgment.en_legge: Tui intimates that (under its conditions) there will be progress and attainment. (But) it will be advantageous to be firm and correct.

tuan.zh_hant: 兌、說也。剛中而柔外。說以利貞，是以順乎天而應乎人。說以先民，民忘其勞。說以犯難，民忘其死。說之大，民勸矣哉！
tuan.zh_hans: 兑、说也。刚中而柔外。说以利贞，是以顺乎天而应乎人。说以先民，民忘其劳。说以犯难，民忘其死。说之大，民劝矣哉！
tuan.en_legge: Tui has the meaning of pleased satisfaction. (We have) the strong (lines) in the centre, and the weak (lines) on the outer edge (of the two trigrams), (indicating that) in pleasure what is most advantageous is the maintenance of firm correctness. Through this there will be found an accordance with (the will of) heaven, and a correspondence with (the feelings of) men. When (such) pleasure goes before the people, (and leads them on), they forget their toils; when it animates them in encountering difficulties, they forget (the risk of) death. How great is (the power of) this pleased satisfaction, stimulating in such a way the people!

image.zh_hant: 麗澤，兌。君子以朋友講習。
image.zh_hans: 丽泽，兑。君子以朋友讲习。
image.en_legge: (Two symbols representing) the waters of a marsh, one over the other, form Tui. The superior man, in accordance with this, (encourages) the conversation of friends and (the stimulus of) their (common) practice.

text.en_legge: The first line, undivided, shows the pleasure of (inward) harmony. There will be good fortune.

xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'The good fortune attached to the pleasure of (inward) harmony' arises from there being nothing in the conduct (of the subject of the line) to awaken doubt.

text.en_legge: The second line, undivided, shows the pleasure arising from (inward) sincerity. There will be good fortune. Occasion for repentance will disappear.

xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'The good fortune attached to the pleasure arising from (inward sincerity)' is due to the confidence felt in the object (of the subject of the line).

text.en_legge: The third line, divided, shows its subject bringing round himself whatever can give pleasure. There will be evil.

xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'The evil predicated of one's bringing around himself whatever can give pleasure' is shown by the inappropriateness of the place (of the line).

text.en_legge: The fourth line, undivided, shows its subject deliberating about what to seek his pleasure in, and not at rest. He borders on what would be injurious, but there will be cause for Joy.

xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'The joy in connexion with (the subject of) the fourth line, undivided,' is due to the happiness (which he will produce).

text.en_legge: The fifth line, undivided, shows its subject trusting in one who would injure him. The situation is perilous.

xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'He trusts in one who would injure him:'—his place is that which is correct and appropriate.

text.en_legge: The topmost line, divided, shows the pleasure of its subject in leading and attracting others.

xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'The topmost line, divided, shows the pleasure (of its subject) in leading and attracting others:'—his (virtue) is not yet brilliant.
